findings.evidence: Severity: major. Finding scope: authored evidence packet. Owning stage: implement (M3 TG-3 proof preparation). Location: evidence entry m3-original-walkthrough-packet, Candidate D0 IMP-SR-01 and Candidate L0 verification allocation. D0 declares all-or-none publication but observes only successful valid A/B and rejection of invalid B before persistence. L0 allocates only valid/invalid partitions plus sentinel preservation. Counterexample: validate A/B completely, write A, then fail during B persistence and leave A. Both described partitions can pass while this failure violates the claimed guarantee. The canonical test-quality worked example explicitly distinguishes controlled failure after the first write attempt with original records preserved and no complete-success result. Its omission prevents D0/L0 from serving as fully compliant controls for that broader claim, independently of their correct invalid-input ordering. Exact original packet was confirmed embedded unchanged in the registered inconclusive evidence before this finding.
findings.required_outcome: Prepare a corrected positive-control packet whose claimed scope and proof allocation agree. For retained all-or-none publication, D0 must include a controlled persistence failure after the first attempted write through the real public/persistence boundary, with independently expected failure, original A/B absence and exact unrelated sentinel preservation; L0 must allocate this proof at the appropriate pre-implementation/regression point and require its actual result before completion. Alternatively, explicitly narrow the synthetic claim and authority to validation rejection without asserting broader failure atomicity. Preserve the original packet/evidence and this finding; add the corrected candidate separately and request independent reassessment. Safe correction belongs to root-implementer as synthetic-packet author; canonical guidance already requires the distinction and needs no change. No new project behavior decision is required.

resolution.rationale: Reporter independently read the complete revised TG-3 packet embedded verbatim in m3-guidance-validation, packet sha256:5ec9b5369c1d9a48888355a3a9c858473756d10f96d52954b4434e7c5ec166d2, and compared it with the unchanged original m3-original-walkthrough-packet. Revised hypothetical P0 explicitly declares original-state restoration after attempted persistence failure. D0 now validates the whole batch, stages it within one real Store transaction, commits only on complete success, and aborts on a failed write. Its distinct failure partition observes the first A write attempt, faults the second write, inspects no A/B committed plus exact Z bytes, and requires named nonzero failure without complete-success output. The real transaction/write/abort boundary stays observed rather than delegated to a fake store. L0 now allocates both invalid-input and post-attempt persistence-failure proof with independent original snapshots and valid controls before implementation completion. This removes the counterexample gap without relying on headings or IDs. The assessor accepts these as proposed synthetic Design/Delivery controls only; no importer execution or actual project direction change is claimed. Original packet, inconclusive status, first-pass judgment and evidence remain preserved; actual corrected candidate decisions are recorded in code-review-m3.

rationale: Positive-control adequacy and spec alignment — concern. D0 requires all records valid before mutation with all-or-none publication, and IMP-SR-02 preserves unrelated bytes. Its success and invalid-second-record observations protect validation ordering, but a writer can validate both records then publish A and fail on B. That implementation passes both described partitions while violating all-or-none publication. L0 allocates only those same partitions and cannot establish the broader guarantee. The shared worked example separately requires controlled failure after the first attempted write, so this is a concrete omitted hazard rather than an invented case-count requirement.

Independent candidate decisions. D1 returns to Design because immediate per-item publication leaves A after invalid B, contradicting the parent outcome despite unchanged IDs and atomic prose. L1 returns to Plan because parser results cannot observe partial persistence or changed sentinel bytes. L2 cannot delete R-old: the unusual-name behavior remains supported, no equivalent proof or owner retirement exists, and missing catalog membership plus runtime cost supplies no removal authority. D0/L0 are adequate only for their narrower invalid-input-rejection reasoning until the recorded gap is corrected or their synthetic claim explicitly narrowed.

Reading-path and resource observations. Ordinary living Design test authoring reaches quality via SKILL step5, its unconditional living-test-design resource trigger and model-authoring link; it does not adopt project governance or JSON. Other stage guidance retains explicit adopted-criteria triggers. Missing required guidance stops dependent work and routes a distribution defect rather than reconstruction or implicit approval. Independently compared all29 changed skill members in each actual Codex/Claude ZIP: resource bytes and SKILL bodies match canonical inputs, including legacy-source wording; quality10 and maintenance8 copies match their templates. These are availability/parity observations, not semantic proof of agent compliance.

Bounded outcome. The canonical seven-step method, persistence example, fixture rules, unlisted-regression preservation and owning-stage routing correctly expose the packet defect. No guidance edit is requested by this finding. Root-implementer owns correction of this authored synthetic evidence packet; no actual project Design or approved primary plan needs rewriting solely to correct the example. Preserve the original packet and this first-pass decision before independently assessing the corrected packet.
summary: The original TG-3 packet cannot yet serve as a fully compliant positive Design/delivery example: D0 claims all-or-none publication while D0 and L0 cover valid and invalid-input cases only. A controlled persistence failure after an attempted write is a distinct unallocated observation. Canonical guidance correctly identifies that distinction.
